claims.text: High-entropy alloys are near-equiatomic, multicomponent alloys.
The proposed alloy is a disordered solid solution.
High-throughput composition adjustment can identify optimal ratios of catalytically active elements.
Transition metals such as Ni, Co, and Mo are catalytically active elements relevant to the proposed HER/HOR alloy.
The catalyst is to be operated in 0.5 M H2SO4 under HER/HOR conditions.
The optimized alloy will retain a homogeneous disordered structure.
A homogeneous disordered structure provides a synergistic distribution of catalytic active sites.
Neighboring atoms in the disordered alloy electronically modify the active sites.
Multiple principal elements synergistically tune the electronic structure of active sites for hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
Optimized hydrogen adsorption and desorption reduce HER and HOR overpotentials.
The proposed multielement alloying effect increases resistance to corrosion and dissolution in acidic media.
The optimized high-entropy alloy will exhibit lower overpotentials than conventional Pt-based or unoptimized alloy catalysts.
The optimized high-entropy alloy will exhibit higher HER and HOR exchange current densities than the baseline catalysts.
The optimized high-entropy alloy will be more durable than conventional Pt-based or unoptimized alloy catalysts under identical testing conditions.
Enhanced performance is expected only within a composition range that preserves a single-phase disordered solid solution.
Phase separation or intermetallic-compound formation may prevent the proposed catalytic enhancement.
